items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was he in any relation to Sugar Johnny? No.

ctx.x: What did he play? Something. Was he Sugar? He played with Black Patty. Sure, you know. What was his last name? No, I'll tell you.

Was he in any relation to Sugar Johnny? No. What branch of the family did he come in? On the daddy's side. On the daddy's side. Well, you've got a lot of cousins in music. Now what about Marrero? That's all first cousins. They're first cousins? Yeah. Yeah. Well, Marrero's on my mother's side. I see. Now you take the Frazier's on my mother's side. And Dave Williams is in my side.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: you had, uh, the Imperial Band, that was, uh, Johnny Smith. That's Sugar Johnny?

ctx.x: Who were the Boys in Blue?

Well, the Boys in Blue, that was Buddy Petit. That's Buddy Petit, well, sometime you'll get Buddy Petit on that, and you had, uh, the Imperial Band, that was, uh, Johnny Smith. That's Sugar Johnny? Sugar Johnny, you understand? And, uh, well, I don't know, it's a good man of Marquette never get together, I believe it'll take me 50 years to get that together. Yeah. Who was in the Golden Rule?
I can't ever keep that band straight.
